column1: # quantity_kinds.tsv — controlled vocabulary for `measurement.quantity_kind` (PLAN.md C.6 and
# I.3: "Production (titer, yield, productivity, specific productivity), physiology (growth rate,
# biomass yield, substrate uptake, fermentation time, oxygen requirement) ... and tolerance").
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS: the column had no vocabulary anywhere. `schema.sql` documented one in a
# trailing comment ("titer | yield | productivity | growth_rate | ..."), the extraction FieldSpec
# offered the same list as free prose, and the promoter checked only that the string was
# non-empty. Measured on the live atlas on 2026-09-24, that produced **21 distinct values over
# 105 rows**, of which 17 are one-offs and several are whole sentences:
#     isobutanol concentration on SC agar permitting growth
#     percent_decrease_in_isobutanol_titer_upon_valine_feeding
#     LC50 (approximate, growth reduced by slightly more than half)
# A sentence in this column is not a kind. Nothing can group by it, no unit rule can be attached
# to it, and two rows measuring the same quantity under different sentences never meet.
# THIS FILE IS LOAD-BEARING, and the distinction it carries is ABSOLUTE vs RELATIVE. A titer is a
# number about one culture. A fold_change is a number about a PAIR — it is meaningless without the
# control it was computed against, and it cannot be converted into a titer, ranked against one, or
# averaged with one. PLAN.md I.2's rule that comparisons happen only within a comparability class
# is the same rule one level down: a relative measurement's class includes its control, so the
# control has to be recoverable from the row. Where it is not, the row says what it measured and
# refuses to say how much.
# WHAT THIS FILE DOES NOT DO: it does not add a CHECK to `measurement.quantity_kind`. SQLite
# cannot add a constraint to an existing column without rebuilding the table, and
# `db/migrations.py`'s rule is that a migration may add and backfill and may not destroy. So the
# vocabulary binds at the two places a value actually enters — the extraction schema
# (`extract/schemas.py`, which now offers this list as a closed choice) and the promoter
# (`curate/promote.py`, which refuses a value outside it rather than storing it) — and
# `query.drift` reports the rows already stored outside it. Remapping those is a curator's call
# and is not performed by any of this.
# Columns:
#   quantity_kind   the closed vocabulary value
#   measure_class   absolute | relative | threshold — see the note column; this is the field that
#                   decides whether a row is interpretable on its own
#   description     what is measured
#   unit_family     the natural unit family, for cross-checking against units.tsv
#   note            what this kind may NOT be aggregated with, and why
#   evidence, confidence
# Evidence honesty, following assay_types.tsv's pass: a row citing only another fermdb document
# (PLAN.md, schema.sql, a stored value) is 'unverified' — citing an internal document is citing
# memory with an extra hop. Nothing here has been checked against a source outside this repo, so
# nothing here is 'high'.
quantity_kind
titer
column3: Concentration of a product in the broth at a stated timepoint.
column5: Interpretable alone. NOT comparable across condition contexts without the facets that differ being named (PLAN.md I.2); a shake-flask titer and a fed-batch titer are different numbers about different experiments.
column6: PLAN.md I.3 "Production (titer, ...)"; 64 of the atlas's 105 rows already use this exact term

column1: yield
column3: Product formed per substrate, as a ratio. Requires `basis` to say consumed or supplied.
column4: mass per mass (g/g) or mol per mol
column5: Interpretable alone ONLY with its basis: g/g-consumed and g/g-supplied are different numbers and papers report both without saying which, which is why `measurement.basis` forbids NULL for a yield. Subject to the theoretical ceiling check of S.3.

column1: productivity
column3: Product formed per unit volume per unit time, averaged over the run.
column5: NOT derivable from titer alone — it needs the fermentation time, and a titer reached in 24 h and in 120 h are the same titer and very different productivities.

column1: specific_productivity
column3: Product formed per unit biomass per unit time.
column5: NOT interconvertible with productivity: one is per volume, the other per cell mass, and they diverge exactly when biomass differs between strains — which is the usual case when comparing an engineered strain to its parent.

column1: growth_rate
column3: Specific growth rate (mu) in the exponential phase.
column5: A tolerance measurement reported as a growth rate at a stated stressor concentration is this kind PLUS an `assay_type` of growth_rate_in_x_percent; the stressor concentration belongs in the condition context, not in this column.

column1: biomass_yield
column5: NOT the same as `yield`, which is product per substrate. A strain can gain biomass yield and lose product yield on the same substrate; collapsing the two terms would hide exactly that trade-off.

column1: substrate_uptake_rate
column3: Rate at which the substrate is consumed.
column4: mass per mass per time (g/gDW/h) or mass per volume per time
column5: Interpretable alone. Pairs with `yield` to give productivity, but the atlas stores what the paper reported and derives nothing here.

column1: fermentation_time
column3: Duration of the run, or time to a stated endpoint.
column5: Not a performance measure on its own; it is the denominator that turns a titer into a productivity, and is stored so that conversion is possible rather than assumed.

column1: consumption
column3: Total amount of substrate consumed over the run.
column5: Distinct from substrate_uptake_rate, which is per unit time and per unit biomass. A total and a rate are not the same quantity.
column6: PLAN.md I.3; the schema.sql trailing comment lists "consumption"

column1: od
column3: Optical density, as printed, at the wavelength the paper states.
column5: NOT a biomass measurement without the paper's own OD-to-gDW factor, which is strain- and instrument-specific. Stored as printed; converting it silently would invent a calibration.
column6: The schema.sql trailing comment lists "od"; 1 stored row uses an OD-based value

column1: inhibitory_concentration
column3: The stressor concentration at which a stated response occurs — IC50, MIC, LC50 and the "grew on agar up to X" readings.
column4: mass per volume (g/L) or percent v/v
column5: A THRESHOLD, not a performance number: it says where a response happens, not how much was produced. The response definition lives in `assay_type` and IC50 / MIC / LC50 are NOT interconvertible with one another (see assay_types.tsv). A row here without an assay_type is not comparable to any other row here.
column6: assay_types.tsv (IC50, MIC); 3 stored rows are threshold readings written as prose

column1: fold_change
column3: A ratio of two measurements, engineered over control. Direction lives in the VALUE, not in the term.
column5: MEANINGLESS WITHOUT ITS CONTROL, and the control must be recoverable from the row. NOT comparable with any absolute kind, never averaged with one, and never ranked against one: a 12-fold increase over a near-zero parent and a 1.2-fold increase over a strong one can describe the same titer. Deliberately ONE signed term rather than fold_increase / fold_decrease / fold_improvement — three terms for one quantity is how a vocabulary stops being able to group.
column6: PLAN.md I.2's comparability rule read one level down; 11 stored rows say fold_increase and 4 more say some variant of it

column1: percent_change
column3: A percentage difference from a control, engineered over control. Direction lives in the VALUE.
column5: MEANINGLESS WITHOUT ITS CONTROL, exactly as fold_change is, and it is the same quantity under a different scaling — but the two are kept apart because converting between them silently changes what a value of "50" means. NOT comparable with any absolute kind. 8 stored rows use some prose variant of this and each names its control only inside the term itself, which is where this vocabulary's absence has cost the most.
column6: PLAN.md I.2; the 8 stored prose variants

column1: unknown
column3: The paper reports a number whose kind does not fit any row above.
column5: The escape hatch, and it must stay available: a curator who cannot classify a number must be able to say so rather than choosing the nearest term. `units.tsv` carries the same escape for the same reason — a forced choice from a closed list is how a list gets silently wrong. A row marked unknown is excluded from every aggregation until it is classified.
column6: units.tsv's 'unknown' precedent ("answer 'unknown' rather than converting into one that is")
